newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- EUROTUNNEL EUTL.PS BACKS WAGON DESIGN

Eurotunnel, the Channel tunnel operator, will next month announce that it is to retain the semi-open wagon system used for freight traffic on its trains. The move comes in spite of fire brigade claims that the design exacerbated a serious blaze in the tunnel in November 1996. An internal Eurotunnel report due to be made public after Easter recommends "common sense changes" to safety systems and enhancements to equipment but gives a "largely clean bill of health" to safety procedures in the tunnel.
-- UK NOT READY FOR EMU, SAYS BARCLAYS' CHIEF

Martin Taylor, the chief executive of the Barclays banking group, said on Tuesday that the UK had not yet achieved sufficient economic convergence with the rest of Europe to participate in Emu, but that it should not prevent the formation of a core Euro-zone involving Germany, France, Austria and the Benelux countries. Taylor added that southern European governments were not ready for the euro and warned that premature participation in Emu at too high an exchange rate could "even ruin some areas".
-- "GREEN" GROUP IN BID FOR OIL LICENCE

Greenpeace lodged a late bid on Tuesday to take part in the government's 17th licensing round for oil and gas exploration on the UK continental shelf. The environmental pressure group is currently campaigning against further oil and gas developments in frontier areas such as the country's newest oil region west of the Shetland Islands. Greenpeace said that its bid, which covers all 127 blocks included in the round, was "a serious initiative" aimed at forcing the government to explain why it was encouraging further oil and gas development when it had committed the country to reducing greenhouse gas emissions from burning fossil fuels.
-- ROBOTICS SECTOR URGED TO FOCUS ON FOOD AND MEDICINE

The Department of Trade and Industry published a report Tuesday urging the UK robotics industry to concentrate its efforts on becoming "a major force" in non-industrial applications such as the medical and food sectors. Though the UK industry has lost its chance to play a significant role in the industrial robot market, the report says that, if it is not neglected, the UK medical robotics industry could become "a major wealth-creating activity". The report also called for the creation of a representative body to co-ordinate robotics activities across the UK.
-- CAR DEALING FRANCHISES "RAVAGED" BY COMPETITION

The number of franchised car dealers in the UK fell by almost 10 percent to 6,574 last year, the biggest fall for a decade, because of fierce competition and restructuring in pursuit of greater efficiency, according to a report from motor trade consultancy Sewells International. The decline came in spite of continuing expansion by some Asian manufacturers, without which Sewells estimates the franchise count would now be close to 6,000. The Ford network registered the greatest decline, with the closure of 22 main dealers and 151 retail dealers. Rover lost 124 retail dealers but added 18 main dealers.
-- TOYOTA CAR WILL RUN ON PETROL AND ELECTRICITY

Japanese automotive giant Toyota announced on Tuesday that it plans to become the first global carmaker to mass-produce a "hybrid" passenger vehicle running on both petrol and electricity. The cost of installing two drive systems has so far dissuaded car manufacturers from producing hybrid vehicles commercially. A 1,500cc petrol engine will propel the Toyota hybrid at normal speeds while simultaneously charging the electric batteries used to provide pollution-free power in cities. Production is due to start within a year.
-- VISA ROLLS OUT ITS NEW CHIP CARD TOOL-KIT

International payment cards consortium Visa has unveiled a new generation tool-kit designed to enable banks to progress from magnetic stripe cards to the chip cards which will become the future standard. The programme includes a new set of technical specifications for banks to develop their own chip applications using the Java computer language. Chip cards will offer multi-function use, including standard credit/debit services, stored value, administering loyalty schemes and having international validity.
-- VOLVO AND TWR JOIN FORCES TO DEVELOP BUS CHASSIS

Swedish automotive group AB Volvo is to combine its bus chassis development activities in a joint venture with Britain's TWR automotive engineering consultancy. The new company will develop chassis for buses and coaches for Volvo, the world's second biggest bus maker. The choice of TWR has surprised some within the industry, although the two companies are also collaborating on the Auto-Nova joint venture to manufacture Volvo sports cars.
-- BMW AHEAD 22 PERCENT AS ROVER IMPROVES

German luxury carmaker BMW has reported a 22 percent increase in first-quarter sales to DM14 billion ($8.3 billion) after the number of units sold rose 8 percent to 285,000. Group chairman Bernd Pischetsrieder said the buoyant figures were due in part to new models such as the 5 series and the Z3 roadster. Sales at Rover, the British carmaker owned by BMW, rose to DM14.9 billion in 1996 compared to DM12.9 billion the previous year. Losses at Rover were cut from DM335 million to DM279 million.
-- FORD SUFFERS 'DRASTIC SETBACK' IN GERMANY

The German arm of US motor giant Ford, Ford-Werke, has announced fresh cost-cutting plans after reporting a pre-tax loss of DM509.9 million ($302 million) for 1996. The loss compares to a profit of DM510.3 million in 1995. According to Ford-Werke chief executive William Boddie, the 'drastic setback' was due largely to a shift in sales away from profitable larger models towards smaller vehicles with lower margins, one-off costs including compensation for early retirement, and to a failure to offset a DM400 million increase in costs and wages with efficiency improvements.
